# Auto-generated rule: quality-gate-wrapper-needs-large-output-buffer-and-env-isolation

Full-gate wrapper tests can fail for harness reasons when verbose npm test output exceeds the default execSync buffer or when outer gate environment variables leak into nested gate runs.

## Evidence
Wave 3 Full Gate retries exposed maxBuffer overflow and inherited TYPECHECK_CMD/TEST_CMD/LINT_CMD/FILES/SESSION_START_REF; runCheck now uses a larger buffer and gate tests clear inherited gate env vars.

## Extension Review (2026-08-17)

Extended `expires-at` 2026-08-18 → 2026-10-01 (+45d, the `fragile-file` TTL from
`LEARNING_TYPE_REGISTRY` in `scripts/lib/learnings/schema.mjs:83`). The env half of the
finding is still a LIVE hazard, not a fixed one — the leak chain is intact end to end:
`scripts/run-quality-gate.mjs:280-287` builds the child env with `TYPECHECK_CMD`,
`TEST_CMD`, `LINT_CMD`, `FILES` and `SESSION_START_REF` all set, and `runCheck`
(`scripts/lib/gates/gate-helpers.mjs:58-62`) calls `execSync(cmd, { encoding, stdio,
maxBuffer })` with **no `env` option**, so the gate's own environment is inherited by
`npm test` → vitest → the gate tests. The only mitigation is per-file boilerplate
(`const env = { ...process.env }; delete env.TYPECHECK_CMD;`), present in exactly 4 files
(`tests/scripts/gates/gate-{full,baseline,incremental,per-file}.test.mjs`) and enforced by
nothing — a 5th gate test file that omits it passes under a bare
`npx vitest run tests/scripts/gates/` and fails only inside the nested full gate. The
buffer half IS fixed structurally (`RUN_CHECK_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024`,
`gate-helpers.mjs:13`), but the rule's env half carries the extension on its own.
